name: Open Foundry
tagline: 25 open-source typefaces, each with a written specimen page naming the licence, the designer and every weight
description:
Open Foundry is a curated catalogue of open-source typefaces. It has run for over a decade, and its own words call it "the leading curated source for open source typefaces".

The catalogue holds 25 families. Among them are Inter, Roboto, Poppins, Oswald, EB Garamond, Work Sans, Archivo, Libre Baskerville, League Gothic and Junicode.

The per-font page is what separates this from a list. Each one gives a written description of the face, a classification, the exact licence, the designer, the person who made the specimen, and every weight with its numeric value. The Inter page names "SIL Open Font License v.1.1", "more than 2000 glyphs covering 147 languages" and weights from 100 to 900.

The home page sets a size in points beside each name, so the grid reads as a specimen sheet rather than as a list of links.
pricing_detail: Free. Every font in the catalogue carries an open licence, and the font page names which one.
agent_guidance:
Read the font page, not the home page, when you need the licence. Each page states the exact licence, such as "SIL Open Font License v.1.1", plus the classification, the designer and every weight.

Use it to check a face you already know. The catalogue is 25 families, so it will not answer a broad search. Use Google Fonts or Fontsource for coverage, and this for a written specimen.

The site publishes no llms.txt and no sitemap. The font pages render real HTML, so a plain fetch returns the description and the licence.
why_it_matters: Most free font lists give a name and a download. This gives a written specimen, a named designer and an exact licence line for every one of its 25 faces, which is what a licence check actually needs.
tier_reason: A decade of curation, and every font page carries a written description, a classification, the exact licence, the designer and the full weight list. Held below S because the catalogue is only 25 families, and the site publishes no llms.txt and no sitemap.

name: Collletttivo
tagline: Italian open-source type collective publishing 16 typefaces, funded by donations
description:
Collletttivo is an Italian open-source type foundry and a network of designers. Its own words: "an Open-Source type foundry and a network of people promoting the practice of type design through mutual exchange and collaboration".

The catalogue holds 16 open-source typefaces. Named on the home page are Borges, Ronzino, Aujournuit, Absans, Coconat, Apfel Grotezk and Sinistre.

The site runs four sections: Typefaces, Resources, Studio and Journal. The Journal carries dated posts, and the newest one is "Erratic Signs, Redesigning mountain languages through type design" from 9 February 2026. Older posts introduce a tool called Toools and a type catalogue called Type Tales.

Donations fund the work. The site states that the collective "lives on thanks to the work of its members and the support of the many downloading and using their typefaces".

The markup carries the line "JavaScript is required", so a reader with scripts off gets nothing.
pricing_detail: Free to download. Donations fund the collective, and the site lists its donors as thanks.
agent_guidance:
Reach for this when a brief wants a face with a point of view rather than a neutral grotesque. The catalogue is 16 typefaces, so read it as a foundry and not as a search index.

Check the licence on the typeface page before you ship. The site calls the whole catalogue open source, but it does not name one licence for every face on the home page.

The site needs JavaScript. The markup carries "JavaScript is required", so a plain fetch returns the shell and the names, and not the full typeface pages. Render it when you need the detail.

Read the Journal for the reasoning behind a release. It is dated and it names the designer of each addition.
why_it_matters: It is a working example of a type collective funded by donations rather than by retail licences, and it publishes the reasoning behind each release in a dated journal.
tier_reason: A real open-source foundry with 16 typefaces, a dated journal and named designers. Held at B because the catalogue is small, the site needs JavaScript to show anything, and it publishes no llms.txt and no single licence statement for the whole catalogue.

name: The League of Moveable Type
tagline: The first open-source font foundry, running since 2009, with 18 free families and a licensing book
description:
The League of Moveable Type opened in February 2009 and calls itself "the original, the first, the open-source font foundry". It started with one font and a manifesto.

The sitemap lists 18 font pages: The Neue Black, Blackout, Chunk, Fanwood, Goudy Bookletter 1911, Junction, Knewave, League Gothic, League Mono, League Script, League Spartan, Linden Hill, Orbitron, Ostrich Sans, Prociono, Raleway, Sniglet and Sorts Mill Goudy. Several of those are now defaults across the web.

The site states the terms plainly: "The whole catalogue of carefully-picked fonts are free to use however and wherever you need, to build on and learn from." Each font page carries an FAQ.

It also publishes a book, Making Sense of Font Licensing, and a manifesto. A team page credits nine people, among them Tre Seals, Barry Schwartz and Micah Rich.

A membership and a set of courses sit beside the free catalogue.
pricing_detail: The 18 fonts are free to use anywhere. A paid membership and a set of courses sit beside them, and the site also sells a book on font licensing.
agent_guidance:
Read https://www.theleagueofmoveabletype.com/sitemap.xml first. It names all 18 font pages, and the home page does not link them.

Reach for League Gothic, League Spartan, Ostrich Sans, Orbitron or Raleway by name. Several are already defaults on Google Fonts, so check whether the project already has the face before you add a second copy.

Read the font page FAQ for the terms. The site states the whole catalogue is free to use anywhere, and each page carries its own FAQ.

Point a licensing question at /books/making-sense-of-font-licensing. It is the site's own guide to the subject.

The site publishes no llms.txt.
why_it_matters: It is the oldest open-source font foundry on the web, and several of its faces became defaults that other catalogues now redistribute. Its licensing book is a rare plain-language source on a subject most font sites avoid.
tier_reason: The first open-source foundry, running since 2009, with 18 faces that are free to use anywhere, an FAQ on every font page, a named team of nine and a book on font licensing. It publishes a sitemap and a robots.txt. Held below S because the catalogue is 18 families, the home page links no font page, and there is no llms.txt.

18 free families including League Gothic and Raleway

name: Tunera Type Foundry
tagline: 20 typefaces from a Paris foundry, every one under the SIL Open Font License
description:
Tunera Type Foundry is a type foundry based in Paris. It publishes 20 typefaces, and every one carries the SIL Open Font License.

The catalogue: Amakan, Ampoule, Azabache, Brassia, Canarina, Choso, Isenheim, Kobata, Lobular, Luperca, Malebolge, Manosque, Nyght Serif, Paysage, Pescante, Picaflor, Piscolabis, Roubaix Industrielle, Tanklager and Teranoptia.

Every font page states the same four terms: free to use, free to distribute, free to modify, and credit Tunera. The site also asks the reader to support the designer.

The site reads in English, French and Spanish.

One defect matters. The bare host tunera.xyz does not answer. Use www.tunera.xyz, which returns the site.
pricing_detail: Free under the SIL Open Font License. The site asks for credit to Tunera and invites support for the designer.
agent_guidance:
Use https://www.tunera.xyz with the www prefix. The bare host tunera.xyz does not answer, so a link without www fails.

Take the whole catalogue as safe for commercial work. All 20 fonts carry the SIL Open Font License, and each page repeats free to use, free to distribute and free to modify.

Credit Tunera in the project. Every font page asks for it, and the OFL does not require it, so it is a request rather than a term.

Reach for it when a brief wants a display face with character. Teranoptia, Malebolge and Roubaix Industrielle are decorative rather than neutral.

The site publishes no llms.txt.
why_it_matters: Twenty OFL faces from one foundry, with the licence and the three freedoms stated on every single page. Most foundries make you hunt for that, and a font licence is the one fact a commercial project cannot get wrong.
tier_reason: 20 typefaces, all under the SIL Open Font License, with the terms repeated on every font page and the site translated into three languages. Held at B because the catalogue is small, the bare domain does not resolve at all, and the site publishes no llms.txt and no sitemap.

name: indestructible type*
tagline: Owen Earl's free font foundry: nine open revivals including Jost, Besley and Bodoni
description:
indestructible type* is a one-person font foundry by Owen Earl. It publishes free typefaces, and most of them are revivals of historic faces.

The catalogue holds nine: Besley, Bodoni, Cooper, Cowboy, Drafting, Gnomon, Jost, Marauder and No Tears. Jost is the widely used one, a geometric sans in the Futura tradition.

The site splits the work into Indestructible Fonts, Experimental Fonts and Coming Soon.

It runs on GitHub Pages from Indestructible-Type/Indestructible-Type.github.io, at 38 stars, with the last push on 31 May 2026.

The domain indestructibletype.com is not the site. It serves a 209-byte page that redirects with a meta refresh to the GitHub Pages address.
pricing_detail: Free. The repository carries no LICENSE file, so read the licence on each font page before commercial use.
agent_guidance:
Link to https://indestructible-type.github.io, not to indestructibletype.com. The .com serves a 209-byte page that redirects by meta refresh, so a fetch of it returns no content.

Reach for Jost when a brief asks for Futura and the budget does not reach a licensed cut. It is the face this foundry is known for.

Check the licence per font. The GitHub repository reports no licence, so do not assume the OFL for every face without reading its page.

The catalogue is nine families. Use it for a specific revival, not for a search.
why_it_matters: Jost alone put this one-person foundry into wide use, and the whole catalogue is historic revivals done carefully rather than a grab bag of free downloads.
tier_reason: Nine careful revivals from one designer, one of which, Jost, is in wide use, and the site is still active with a push in May 2026. Held at B because the catalogue is small, the GitHub repository carries no LICENSE file, and the .com domain is only a meta refresh rather than the site.

name: fontain
tagline: 48 libre fonts in one browser comparison sheet, classified and set in live editable text
description:
fontain calls itself "a font-collection (and a font-collection-system)". It shows 48 libre fonts on one page, each set in the same editable line of text.

Eight classifications filter the sheet: Calligraphic, Blackletter, Serif, Sans-Serif, Script, Decorative, Monospaced and Pixel. A size control and a reset control sit beside them.

The point is comparison. You type once and read the same words in 48 faces, rather than opening 48 specimen pages.

The collection holds well-known libre faces such as Playfair Display, Fira Code, Inconsolata, Source Code Pro, PT Serif, Raleway, Junicode and Dancing Script, beside rarer ones such as Manifont Grotesk, Pressuru, GrobeDeutschmeister and osifont.

The source is public at lafkon/fontain with 49 stars. The last push was 31 January 2023, so the project is dormant.
pricing_detail: Free. The collected fonts carry their own libre licences. The tool itself has no LICENSE file in its repository.
agent_guidance:
Send a person here to compare, not an agent to search. The value is 48 faces set in one line of your own text on one page, which a fetch cannot use.

Do not treat the tool as reusable. The repository lafkon/fontain carries no LICENSE file, and the last push was January 2023.

Check each font's own licence at its source. fontain collects libre faces but does not state a licence per font on the sheet.

Use the eight classifications to narrow a brief: Calligraphic, Blackletter, Serif, Sans-Serif, Script, Decorative, Monospaced and Pixel.
why_it_matters: It answers the one question a font list cannot: how do these faces look set in my words, side by side. Forty-eight of them on one page, with no account and no upload.
tier_reason: A clear single-purpose comparison sheet for 48 libre faces, with eight classifications and live editable text. Held at C because the project is dormant with no push since January 2023, the repository carries no LICENSE file, the sheet states no licence per font, and the collection is small next to Google Fonts or Fontsource.

name: Supa Fonts
tagline: Free font download site with browser font generators, and no licence stated on the catalogue
description:
Supa Fonts is a free font download site with a set of browser font generators beside it. Its own words: "SupaFonts is library of underrated fonts & font generators".

The catalogue divides into Display, Elegant, Groovy, Sans Serif, Serif, Sports and a category named Taylor Swift Fonts. A Font Generator section sits beside them.

Named faces include Bebas Neue, Alte Haas Grotesk, Caviar Dreams, Boska, Gambarino, Cinzel Decorative and Bodoni XT.

One thing is missing, and it is the thing that matters for a font. The catalogue pages do not state a licence. The site carries a DMCA link in the footer, which tells you how takedown requests are handled rather than what you may ship.

The markup leaks its own template. Strings such as `{title}` and a commented-out block appear in the served HTML.
pricing_detail: Free to download. The site states no licence for the fonts it serves, and the footer carries a DMCA link.
agent_guidance:
Do not use this for a commercial project without checking the font elsewhere. The catalogue states no licence, and a font with no stated licence is the one asset that can stop a launch.

Take a name from here, then verify it at its real source. Bebas Neue, Boska and Gambarino all come from foundries that publish their own terms.

Prefer Google Fonts, Fontshare, Velvetyne or Use & Modify for the same job. Each of those names a licence for every face.

The font generators produce styled Unicode text, not font files. That output breaks screen readers, so keep it out of a product interface.
why_it_matters: It shows what a free font catalogue looks like without a licence column, which is the failure mode this corpus records licences to avoid.
tier_reason: A working free font catalogue with generators and a clear category structure. Held at C because it states no licence for any font, which is the one fact a commercial project needs, its footer offers a DMCA link in place of terms, and the served HTML leaks unrendered template strings.
